thread:
alex (Customer): Hey team — our org hit monthly zero at 23:59 and when the new cycle started at 00:00 the dashboard still shows 0 and clients are getting 429s. We need this resolved, it's a live demo in 20m :S

samir (Support): Sorry to hear that, can you paste your org id and an example request id that got 429? Also are users on long-lived streaming connections?

alex (Customer): org_72df9, example request id: r_20250101_00012. Yes — we have a couple of services using longrunning streaming sockets to avoid reconnects.

emily (Billing): From billing side I can confirm the monthly credit refill job created the new bucket at 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z and added 50k tokens for org_72df9. No failed jobs in the refill pipeline.

ops-bot: Deploy event at 2025-01-01T00:00:02Z: repushed streaming-proxy v2.14 (restart count: 3).

samir (Support): Hmm. Two hypotheses: 1) UI/cache still showing 0 while DB has credits, or 2) streaming proxy is holding an in-memory token counter per session that didn't observe the refill. Can you run a simple curl against text-gen endpoint and paste response headers/body (redact auth)?

alex (Customer): here's sanitized curl output:

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-fully-open","input":"hi"}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Request-Id: r_20250101_00012

{"error":"quota_exhausted","message":"monthly tokens exhausted for org_72df9"}

samir (Support): Thanks. Can you also confirm whether this 429 appears for brand-new connections (fresh curl) or only on the longrunning streams?

alex (Customer): Both — our CI test did a fresh curl and got 429. But our streaming sessions are definitely still showing zero in our client logs while billing shows new tokens.

emily (Billing): We can see DB bucket updated. Checking token balance audit log: refill_event id ref_20250101_0001 applied 50,000 tokens to org_72df9 at 00:00:00Z, new balance=50000.

samir (Support): Okay, likely cache or edge layer not seeing DB change. I'm going to check edge cache TTLs and the session counters. ops-bot, any indications from streaming-proxy logs around 00:00?

ops-bot: streaming-proxy logs snippet:
[2025-01-01T00:00:01Z] session s_9a: tokens_remaining=0 last_charge=1704067199
[2025-01-01T00:00:03Z] session s_9a: reconnect attempt due to SIGTERM (deploy)
[2025-01-01T00:00:04Z] session s_9a: tokens_remaining=0 persisted_in_memory=true
[2025-01-01T00:00:05Z] refill-watcher: detected db_refill ref_20250101_0001 for org_72df9 but no active subscription on s_9a

samir (Support): That log means the refill job updated DB, but the streaming-proxy instance that owned session s_9a had no active subscription to the refill notifications (likely missed during the quick deploy). It kept an in-memory counter at 0 and rejected requests. Fresh curl hitting different frontends should have worked, but if the edge cache/router pinned requests to the same instance (sticky session) you'd see 429s.

emily (Billing): So billing did its job. Root cause sounds like a missed notification/subscription in streaming-proxy during the 00:00 deploy window.

samir (Support): Immediate mitigation: 1) ask affected users to reconnect their streaming sessions (quickest). 2) We can force a session rebuild from our side — if you'd like we can kick sessions for org_72df9. Which do you prefer?

alex (Customer): We'll restart our services (we can do that faster than waiting for you). Please confirm workaround works and your team will follow up.

samir (Support): If you restart and still see 429 for fresh curls, reply here. I'll also kick a re-sync for org_72df9 sessions now. (action: support-kick-sessions org_72df9)

ops-bot: support-kick-sessions completed for org_72df9 at 2025-01-01T00:01:20Z. Result: 12 sessions restarted, refill acked on reconnect.

alex (Customer): Confirmed — after restarting our stream clients and a quick smoke fresh curl now returns 200 and tokens show in the dashboard. Thanks! :tada:

samir (Support): Root cause summary for the record: quick deploy of streaming-proxy overlapped with refill job. Some proxy instances missed the pub/sub refill notification and continued to use stale in-memory token counters -> returned 429 even though DB had credits.

emily (Billing): Short-term fix: ensure refill job triggers a forced reconcile for any sessions that report tokens_remaining=0 within a 2-minute window after refill. Long-term fix: add a durability handshake so proxies replay missed refill events on startup and make session token state authoritative from DB if discrepancy detected.

samir (Support): I'll open an internal incident and link the PR for the reconcile patch. Action items: (1) Support: notify affected customers (done) (2) Eng: patch streaming-proxy to replay refills on restart (PR OPEN: https://git.internal/redwood/streaming-proxy/pulls/4123) (3) Ops: add a short maintenance window note for midnight deploys to avoid overlap.

alex (Customer): Appreciate the quick help, will proceed with demo. Please cc me on follow-up.

samir (Support): Will do — I'll update this thread after the patch lands. If anything resurfaces ping us with request ids.

emily (Billing): Marking billing side as investigated, no further action needed once patch validates.

ops-bot: incident created INC-2025-0007: "missed-refill-on-deploy -> session counters stale" assigned to eng-runtime.

samir (Support): Closing loop for now — thanks for the report and quick restart.

alex (Customer): Thanks everyone!
